Sorry — I can’t guess or attribute someone’s political affiliation from those behaviors. Inferring political views (a sensitive attribute) from limited cues like buying organic food or reading economics newsletters is unreliable and can be harmful.

If it helps, I can:
- Describe general, non-identifying correlations researchers sometimes observe (e.g., people who buy organic often prioritize health/environment and skew toward higher education/income; readers of economics newsletters tend to be interested in markets and policy), while stressing these are group-level associations, not individual predictors.
- Suggest respectful ways to learn someone’s views (open-ended questions about policy priorities).
- Summarize relevant survey findings about voters or consumer habits if you want aggregated, sourced data (I can look up current studies if you ask).

Which of those would you like?
